extension.summary: Auto-applies XStream Player + TMDb Bingie Helper fixes
extension.description: Runs once at Kodi startup. Wires TMDb Bingie Helper's player config to XStream Player, patches known XStream Player bugs (series ID lookup, provider name-prefix cleanup, EPG notification spam), and sets XStream Player as the default player so Discover/search play directly without a chooser dialog. Safe to re-run — checks before changing anything, and will not touch a different XStream Player version than the one these patches were built against, to avoid corrupting it.
extension.news: 1.5.1 - Fixed the "Select Item" picker showing up-to-4 unrelated candidates (other shows sharing part of the name, wrong regions) every time you picked an episode to play/search from Discover. Root cause: player_config.json matched the show by name AND an exact year, but the year TMDb sends for an episode-level request is that episode's own air year (which varies season to season), not the show's debut year your catalog is labeled with -- so it essentially never matched, and always fell back to showing you everything. Now matches by name and any 4-digit year with a "(US)" region tag (dropping the exact-year requirement), which correctly narrows to just the real matches and lets the existing silent-first-match behavior take over -- no more picker for this case. 1.5.0 - New (experimental): Discover's episode tiles (Season view, e.g. reached via search or the new Back button) now show real watched/progress indicators, instead of always appearing unwatched. Root cause was the same as the earlier "Play Season 1: Episode 1" bug: those tiles' watched-status comes from a Trakt.tv lookup, and nothing in this setup scrobbles there. This time the fix patches TMDb Bingie Helper's own trakt.py directly (a new, separate patch target alongside XStream Player, version-gated the same way) to check XStream Player's real watch history first -- via a new discover_watch_export mode, cached per show so it's one cross-addon lookup per season view, not per episode -- falling through to the original Trakt-based lookup when there's no match, so nothing else about Discover changes. Please test and report back. 1.4.2 - Confirmed working on real devices: the Discover-aware Back button (1.4.0) now lands correctly on the right season's episode list. This adds proper breadcrumb navigation on top of it -- pressing Back a second time, from that season's episode list, now goes up to Discover's "all seasons" page for the show instead of exiting straight out, matching normal Kodi folder-browsing behavior. Works by visiting the show's seasons page first and then drilling into the specific season as a second navigation step, so Kodi's own container history naturally has the right parent, rather than jumping straight to the season directly. 1.4.1 - Removed a stray diagnostic notification ("Autoplay debug: pos=X dur=Y -- not near end") that was firing on nearly every series episode stop. It was meant to be temporary and was believed removed back in 1.3.3, but a background-service revert during a later edit silently restored it without being caught until now. Also checked for and confirmed no other previously-removed diagnostics came back the same way. 1.4.0 - New (experimental): pressing Back/Escape while a series episode from this add-on is playing now stops it and jumps to that show's season in Discover, instead of just returning to whatever screen was open before playback started. Works by reusing Discover's own search to find the show, then locating the matching season within its listing -- everything else (movies, live TV) is unaffected, falling back to a plain stop exactly like Kodi's own default Back-during-playback behavior. This needs a Kodi restart to take effect (keymaps only load at startup), and landing on the exact previously-playing episode (not just the right season) isn't implemented yet -- please test and report back what actually happens, since this couldn't be fully verified without a live device. 1.3.9 - Fixed a second Continue Watching issue and a Discover issue, both from the same root cause: Continue Watching tiles were still landing on a TMDb Bingie Helper show-info screen for some clicks even after 1.3.7, traced to using the wrong Kodi info label (ListItem.Path excludes the query string; needed ListItem.FileNameAndPath, which actually contains it) -- fixed. Separately, Discover's TV show info screen always showed "Play Season 1: Episode 1" no matter how much had actually been watched, because that button's data comes from a Trakt.tv lookup and XStream Player never scrobbles there. Repointed it at a new XStream Player mode that uses its own real watch history instead, so it now offers a genuine "Resume SxEy" (or the next episode, once finished) when one exists, falling back to the old Season 1 Episode 1 default otherwise. 1.3.8 - New: searching/browsing back to a show you've already started now shows a "Resume S3E2 - Title" (or "Play Next" once that episode is finished) shortcut right above the season list, instead of always dropping you at Season 1 with no memory of where you left off. Picks up the most recently watched episode from that show's own watch history; if it was finished, jumps to the next episode instead (rolling into the next season if it was the season finale); if the whole series is finished, no shortcut shows and it's just the normal season list. 1.3.7 - Fixed Continue Watching tiles opening a TMDb Bingie Helper show-info screen instead of playing/resuming directly. Root cause: Bingie skin's shared onclick handler for every Home widget row shows an info screen whenever a clicked item comes from any add-on at all, which is true for Continue Watching's own directly-playable tiles too -- there was no way to distinguish "play this specific thing" from "browse into this show." Now excludes XStream Player's own direct single-stream URLs specifically, so Continue Watching plays straight through while every other row (Trending, New Arabic TV Shows, etc.) keeps showing info first as before. 1.3.6 - Case closed on the wrong-episode report: with Kodi debug logging temporarily on, the full trace showed TMDb Bingie Helper correctly matching S3E23 to the right provider stream id and Kodi's player opening exactly that URL -- and the wrong episode's video still played. That's conclusive: the IPTV provider's backend serves the wrong content for that specific stream id, correctly labeled but wrongly assigned on their end. Nothing either add-on does could catch or fix that. Removes the v1.3.4/1.3.5 diagnostic logging now that it's answered the question. 1.3.5 - v1.3.4's log confirmed xtream_season() itself returns a clean, complete, contiguous 25-episode list for The Office S3 with no gaps or duplicates -- so the add-on's own data is correct, and whatever picks the wrong one is downstream (Discover/TMDb Bingie Helper's own title-text matching). Expands the log to also print each episode's index, provider episode_num, and full title, so the provider's own claimed numbering can be checked directly against which episode actually plays. 1.3.4 - New lead on the wrong-episode/missing-episode report: it only happens via Discover (TMDb Bingie Helper), not when browsing this add-on directly -- confirmed by the reporting user, which rules out an IPTV provider data problem and points at the two add-ons' integration instead (Discover drives a generic JSON-RPC-based folder-matching engine in TMDb Bingie Helper, a separate add-on this project doesn't patch). Adds a log line to xtream_season() recording every call's series/season/profile and exactly how many episodes with which ids it returned, so a Discover-triggered call can be directly compared against a native-browse call for the same show/season. 1.3.3 - Removes the v1.3.2 diagnostic notification. It did its job: confirmed (by the reporting user) that the add-on correctly requests the clicked episode's title/id/stream, but the IPTV provider serves a different episode's video content for that id (e.g. requesting S3E23 plays S3E22). That's a data problem on the provider's backend, not something fixable here -- no further app-side change for this report. 1.3.2 - Diagnostic aid for a reported bug where a clicked/searched-to episode consistently plays the one before it (e.g. clicking S3E9 actually plays S3E8), even on a fresh, never-watched episode. Code review of the episode list and search-to-series flow found no off-by-one -- each row's title and its stream URL come from the exact same provider data in the same loop iteration -- so this adds an on-screen notification the instant playback starts, showing exactly what was requested (title, episode id, stream id), to tell apart "the add-on asked for the wrong episode" from "the add-on asked correctly and the IPTV provider served the wrong content for that id." No behavior change. 1.3.1 - Diagnostic aid for TV show autoplay (v1.2.5) not triggering on some devices: since exactly why differs by device, this adds an on-screen notification whenever a series episode ends, showing the reason (playing the next episode, or the raw pos/dur values seen if it decided not to). No behavior change -- purely visibility, so the real cause on affected devices can be seen directly instead of guessed at. Will be quieted down again once confirmed working broadly. 1.3.0 - New: cross-device watch progress sync. Resume points, finished items, watch history, and watched movies/episodes now sync between every device you run this add-on on, using a private GitHub Gist under your own GitHub account as storage (nothing shared with anyone else, nothing hosted by the developer). Opt-in and off by default -- enable it and paste a GitHub personal access token (gist scope) into this add-on's own Settings on each device you want synced together; the first device creates the Gist, every other device using the same token finds and joins it automatically. Runs on the existing 5-minute recheck cycle, merging by each entry's own timestamp so the most recent watch/progress from any device wins. 1.2.5 - Fixed TV show autoplay: "Auto play next episode" (already on by default) queued the next episode onto Kodi's own video playlist, expecting Kodi to auto-advance into it once the current one ended -- that never actually continued here, so playback just stopped and dropped back to the episode list or Home. The next episode is now launched directly by the same playback monitor that already tracks resume position, the moment the current one finishes (not on an early manual stop), through the same profile/server credentials as the episode that was just playing. 1.2.4 - Finished movies/episodes now drop out of Continue Watching on their own. Previously, once you got near the end of something, the resume point was just deleted -- with nothing recorded to say it was actually finished, so a fresh watch (0% progress, no resume point) could look the same as one you'd just completed, and re-appear in the list. history.py now records a durable "finished" marker at that same near-the-end moment, and Continue Watching filters those out; rewatching something clears its finished marker so it can show up as in-progress again. 1.2.3 - Two Continue Watching fixes: posters now always prefer the clean TMDb/provider poster over whatever raw icon got saved at play time (previously only used as a fallback when nothing was saved at all, which let odd, badly-cropped episode stills through for some shows), and episode tiles now show "Season X - Episode Y" in the hero panel again -- extracted for free from the raw provider name before it gets cleaned for display, so cleaning the messy name no longer means losing which episode this actually is. 1.2.2 - New Arabic Movies/TV Shows rows still not showing on some devices (e.g. a user's Android TV box, despite an identical skin version) even after reinstalling: the patch matched all 4 widget variables (2 slots x Content/Name) as one combined block, so any single mismatch anywhere in that block -- even a harmless whitespace difference -- silently failed all 4 together. Each variable is now matched and patched independently, so a partial mismatch no longer blocks everything, and the log now names exactly which variable failed if one still does. 1.2.1 - Episode lists (e.g. opening a show's season) now show per-episode watch progress as a strip on the tile: a full bar for completed episodes (already worked, driven by watch history), and now also a partial bar for episodes stopped partway through, using the real saved resume position -- previously only fully-watched episodes showed anything. The add-on now also patches XStream Player's history.py (a new file, alongside addon.py) to add the lookup this needed. 1.2.0 - Fixed the white focus-selector border disappearing specifically on Continue Watching tiles: the Home screen's fixed focus-frame required a non-empty ListItem.Label to show at all, which Continue Watching tiles intentionally don't have (no title text). Removed that requirement from all 9 style-variant conditions so the border now shows consistently on every row. 1.1.9 - Two fixes: the dark bottom panel visible on every tile even with no title text was the title-panel background rendering regardless of whether there's a label -- now suppressed whenever the label is empty. Also switched the progress bar from yellow to the skin's own BingieProgressBarColor (already Netflix red, same color the existing hero-panel resume bar uses), instead of a hardcoded color. 1.1.8 - Continue Watching now shows clean TMDb/provider-metadata names and posters instead of the raw (often messy) provider name saved at play time -- e.g. "Dexter: Resurrection" instead of "AR-SUBS: Dexter: Resurrection (2025) (US)". Cache-only lookups (movies via the existing per-item VOD info cache, series via the already-cached catalog list), so this never blocks on a fresh network call during a Home load; falls back to a provider-prefix-stripped version of the raw name when no cached match exists yet. 1.1.7 - Fixed 1.1.6: the new progress bar never actually showed on tiles, because it was painted before the poster's title-panel overlay, which sits on top and hid it completely. Moved it to render after that overlay instead (a separate insertion point in widget_layout_poster, not inside the poster panel itself), so it now shows correctly. 1.1.6 - Continue Watching redesign: movies and episodes are now mixed into one chronological list (most recently watched first) instead of grouped/split by type; item names are no longer shown as text; and a thin yellow progress bar now renders on each tile instead of a percentage label, matching a Netflix-style look. The bar is deliberately approximate, not exact. 1.1.5 - Fixed 1.1.4: the New Arabic Movies/TV Shows rows never actually appeared, because they were inserted into script-skinshortcuts-includes.xml, which gets silently regenerated by script.skinshortcuts's own build process (confirmed: wiped within minutes on a real device). Now repurposes the existing 2nd/3rd Home widget slots instead, the same persistent mechanism Continue Watching already uses successfully. 1.1.4 - Added two new Home screen rows, "New Arabic Movies" and "New Arabic TV Shows", pulling directly from specific catalog categories (this setup's "افلام عربية حديثة" and "يعرض الآن عربي"), positioned right after Continue Watching. 1.1.3 - The 1.1.0 Continue Watching fix only reached the Movies/TV Show category pages, not the actual Home screen -- those turned out to be a completely separate widget mechanism from Home's own. Home's real first row (already designed to show "in progress" content, same as the category-page rows) now points at XStream Player's combined continue-watching feed (movies and episodes together) when the local library is empty. 1.1.2 - Fixed two Continue Watching issues: the single-type Movie/TV Show Hub rows were still showing an unnecessary "Movies"/"Series" section-divider tile meant only for a combined list, and items with no recorded icon (common for older watch-history entries) showed a blank generic placeholder instead of any thumbnail at all -- movies now check the small per-item info cache first, everything else falls back to a proper default icon. 1.1.1 - Fixed a variable-shadowing bug in movie/series category browsing: a cast-list loop reused the same variable name as the item's own title, silently overwriting it with the last actor's name. This corrupted favorites labels, watch history, and even the played title/OSD for any movie/show with cast data, whenever it was opened by browsing a category (search results were unaffected). Fixes garbled entries like a cast list showing up as a "movie name" in Continue Watching. 1.1.0 - Adds a real "Continue Watching" home screen banner. The Bingie skin's home page already has Movie/TV Show rows designed to show in-progress content, but they only read Kodi's local library, which stays empty for a plugin-only IPTV setup, so they fell back to generic TMDb "Trending" placeholders instead of anything personal. Those rows now use XStream Player's own continue-watching data (movies and episodes, with real resume position, across all profiles) so what's actually still-in-progress on the IPTV catalog shows up right on Home. 1.0.9 - Arabic search results were showing broken-looking "Series"/"Live TV" tiles mixed into the poster grid -- those were the combined search's own section dividers, not designed for this grid layout. Arabic search now gets dedicated Movies and Series rows instead of one mixed list, matching how the skin already presents other search results. Migrates automatically from the 1.0.6 single-block patch. 1.0.8 - Episode lists were showing a blank/generic thumbnail whenever a provider has no per-episode still (common for many Arabic-language series) -- episodes now fall back to the show's own poster. Also fixed the previous 1.0.7 fanart fallback to use the real backdrop image the provider actually supplies (confirmed present for both movies and series) instead of stretching the poster. 1.0.7 - Search result info screens (movies and series) were showing a blank backdrop and no plot/creator text, since XStream Player's own search never set a fanart image or series plot on result items. Now falls back to the poster as a backdrop (Xtream's API has no separate wide image) and fills in the plot text that was already being fetched but unused. 1.0.6 - Typing Arabic into the main search box now searches your IPTV catalog directly (movies, series, and live channels) instead of TMDb, since TMDb rarely has Arabic-language IPTV content indexed at all. English/Latin search is unchanged. Patches the Bingie skin's search include by exact content match, so it safely no-ops instead of risking corruption if a skin update changes that section. 1.0.5 - Fixed the Live TV home shortcut sometimes disappearing after a full restart (script.skinshortcuts can resync its own shortcuts file shortly after boot and silently undo our addition). All checks now recheck and self-heal every 5 minutes for the life of the Kodi session, not just once at startup. 1.0.4 - Fixed Live TV guide/search always being empty: vendors the "defusedxml" library so epg.py's own safer XML parser is used instead of its fallback, which wrongly rejected any XMLTV feed with a standard DOCTYPE (nearly all of them). Also adds a "Live TV" home menu shortcut automatically if the skin's shortcuts are set up. 1.0.3 - Fixed wrong-show matches for series with multiple regional/year variants sharing a name (e.g. "The Office" US 2005 vs the 2024 AU reboot) by requiring an exact showname+year match before falling back to a picker, same as the movie fix 1.0.2 - Fixed a crash on Android when backing up/replacing addon.py (shutil.copy2's metadata copy is refused by Android's storage layer; switched to a plain content copy) 1.0.1 - If the fix-check itself crashes, it now shows the full error directly on screen (no log file/uploader needed) 1.0.0 - Initial release
